Yes. Thank you, Saptarshi. First of all, good evening, everyone. It's a pleasure speaking to all of 
you. I will -- in terms of sequencing, I'll maybe first cover a few business numbers and then later 
on take on the profitability part. So business momentum continues to be quite strong. During the 
quarter, we saw a healthy growth in both advances and deposits. However, the key development 
during the quarter was the FCNR mobilization under the RBI scheme. 
 
So let me start with giving some numbers first on that front. During the quarter, the bank 
mobilized INR34,390 crores, which is about USD3.6 billion of FCNR(B) deposit under this 
scheme. This constituted about 10% of the overall deposit that we have at September 30, 2026. 
Against this, we also extended leverage of USD2.6 billion, which is in about INR25,000 crores 
to NRI customers. If we see on the basis of these loans, then this constituted about 7% of the 
overall loan book at September 30, 2026. 
 
At mobilization of USD3.6 billion, the bank garnered about 2.7% of the overall mobilization the 
country received under this scheme. This is about 1% higher than our NRI deposit share, which 
was this pre-FCNR announcement. As part of the exercise, we also obtained our debut 
international rating from S&P and CareEdge. Happy to report that we got an investment-grade 
rating for the bank on this front. 
 
On the back of the ratings, we also did a debut bond issuance. We almost raised close to $1 
billion of bonds. The actual number was US$ 950 million, and these were raised from the 
offshore IBU branch from marquee international investors. Since this was a specific opportunity 
during the current quarter, wherever relevant, I will try to give out numbers with and without 
FCNR to keep underlying trends comparable with the previous quarters. 
 
Moving on to loans. That registered a strong growth of 30.1% on a Y-o-Y basis and 13.6% on a 
Q-on-Q basis, including FCNR, and that book has now reached about INR3.47 lakh crores. If 
we exclude the FCNR(B) backed loans, the loan assets on a gross of IBPC basis grew by 22.2% 
on a Y-o-Y basis and 5.7% on a Q-on-Q basis and was about INR3.29 lakh crores. The 
incremental growth on the loan side during the quarter was primarily driven by mortgage, vehicle 
loans, consumer loans and a slightly faster growth in business banking and wholesale loans, 
which individually grew by more than 30% on a Y-o-Y basis. 
 
The MFI book saw a marginal increase during the quarter. That book now stands at INR6,825 
crores and about 2% of the overall funded assets. 97% of the book is now covered under the

SMA across product classes. We give a fair degree of disclosure in the investor presentation

19 basis points from 1.51% reported in Q1 to 1.32% in Q2 and by 9 bps if we exclude FCNR

to 0.40%. If we exclude the FCNR backed loans, the net NPA ratio would be 0.43% as against 
0.44% reported in the previous quarter. 
 
Further drill down, if we look for now the retail, agri and the MSME book, the GNPA ratio here 
improved from 1.4% to 1.24% and to 1.36% if we exclude again FCNR backed loans from the 
equation. Moving on, the collection efficiency for the current bucket for retail continues to hold 
well. It has been now stable around the 99.5% for many quarters. 
 
The SMA-1 and SMA-2 book for the retail was at 0.72% in Q2 from 0.77%, which we saw in 
the previous quarter. SMA 1 and 2 for microfinance further normalized to 0.6% from 0.7% in 
the previous quarter. At an overall bank level, SMA 1 and 2 reduced by 4 basis points to 0.58%. 
The net slippage ratio for the quarter was stable at about 1.6%. 
 
Moving on to deposits. Total deposits, which is customer deposits plus certificate of deposits 
that reached at INR3.48 lakh crores. The growth was about 25.9% on a Y-o-Y basis and 11.8% 
on a Q-on-Q basis. If I just talk of customer deposits that has crossed INR3.4 lakh crores. It grew 
by 26.9% on a Y-o-Y basis and 14% on a Q-on-Q basis. 
 
This also included FCNR. And if we exclude FCNR deposits, customer deposits grew by 14.1% 
on a Y-o-Y basis. But here is where we slightly calibrated the growth because we got strong 
FCNR inflows during the current quarter. So this was more a conscious strategy which we 
followed during the course of the quarter. 
 
As a result, we did reduce the bulk deposit ratio from 17.1% to 13.9% in the current quarter and 
also repaid certain certificate of deposits as it came up for maturity. If I talk of CASA deposits, 
that grew to now INR1.66 lakh crores. The growth on a Y-o-Y basis was 19.8%, while the CASA 
ratio for the quarter came to 47.6%, this was lower because of the FCNR deposit mobilization 
in the denominator. The average CASA ratio still, I would say, was healthy at about 48.4%. 
 
If I move on to profitability, happy to report that the profit has remained above INR1,000 crores 
for the second consecutive quarter, and the profit for the quarter stands at INR1,045 crores, 
which is an improvement of about 196.5% on a Y-o-Y basis, while it was marginally down as 
we had reported higher treasury income in the previous quarter. 
 
We have also given in the presentation our numbers on a core PAT basis. When I mean core 
PAT, that excludes trading gains for all the periods and also certain one-off items, which we had 
called out in the previous quarters like the impact of the fraud incident, some income tax refunds 
and interest we had come in the previous quarter. The core profit and these details are given in

21.1% Y-o-Y increase reported in the previous quarter. The net interest margin for the quarter 
was 5.58% as compared to 5.90% in the previous quarter, excluding the income tax refund, 
which we have reported. 
 
Now I will talk about why was the moderation in NIM during the current quarter. The NIMs 
moderated because of, I would say, 3 or 4 factors. One was the FCNR, which I would say was 
the primary reason. Since this came into the denominator, we had an impact of about 16 basis 
points on this FCNR-backed lending. Second, because we have mobilized strong, I would say, 
FCNR deposit flows, we, in the interim also parked such liquidity in low-yielding treasury 
instruments and nostro balances that had an impact on NIM of 7 basis points.  
Then there were also impacts because of change in asset mix because we have grown wholesale 
banking and business banking at a faster pace. That had an impact of 5 basis points. And last is 
the day count convention impact because this quarter had 92 days vis-a-vis 91 days in the 
previous quarter. So to summarize, 16 bps is because of FCNR lending, 7 bps is because of 
excess liquidity, 4 bps is because of day count convention and 5 bps is because of other asset 
mix changes. 
 
The one point which I want to sort of also put across is that the margin impact on FCNR should 
not be viewed in isolation as because FCNR comes in the denominator, it correspondingly also 
reduces operating expenses and credit costs related to assets. And hence, we have estimated that 
the overall impact on the ROA could be very minimal as low as 2 basis points. 
 
Pursuant to the FCNR scheme, we also have estimated an additional benefit of 1%, including 
statutory benefits, which could accrue to us if we compare this with a normal deposit, which we 
would have raised otherwise, if these FCNR flows were not there. This FCNR deposit also would 
not consume capital. Hence, whatever we earn, which I mentioned of 1%, that increases my NII, 
that increases my profitability, that increases my ROE, EPS and all of these numbers. 
 
Just in terms of how do we see NIMs going forward, we see this recovering to approximately 
5.8% by Q4 as some of these excess liquidity would have been definitely put to use by them and 
also the expected repo rate increase, which we also are factoring for the course of the year. 
 
Moving on to fee and other income. We saw a healthy growth that increased by about 24.5% on 
a Y-o-Y basis compared to 22.9% in Q1. We have given details of the fee composition in the 
investor presentation. As a result of the increase in the NII and the fee, the total income, 
excluding trading gains for Q2 on a Y-o-Y basis was a growth of 21.9% versus 21.5% reported 
in Q1. During the quarter, the treasury gains were modest at about INR11 crores as compared to 
INR181 crores reported for Q1, which was largely due to the hardening of the G-SEC yields 
during the quarter.

Moving on, the opex for the quarter was at INR5,942 crores. This grew by 16% on a Y-o-Y basis 
and by 3.7% on a sequential basis. The increase of 3.7% corresponds to an increase in core 
income growth of about 4.6% on a sequential basis. As a result, the cost-to-income ratio, 
excluding trading gains, improved by 57 basis points on a sequential basis to 70.2% and was, in 
fact, 358 bps lower on a Y-o-Y basis. 
 
Operating jaw, which is the growth between the total income and the opex, that continues to 
improve. In fact, for the quarter, it stood at 592 basis points. And for H1, it stands at 553 basis 
points. If you remember, we had guided for an upwards of 500 basis points, which we would 
endeavor to maintain, and we are broadly on track on that front. 
 
As a result, the incremental cost-to-income ratio was about 55% for H1. And that has also 
resulted in some of the opening of the jaws, which I sort of spoke of slightly earlier. If I talk of 
operating profit of the quarter, that saw a healthy increase of 38.5% on a Y-o-Y basis and 6.6% 
on a sequential basis. So for 3 quarters in a row now, we are getting an operating profit increase 
of upwards of 30%. 
 
Moving on to provisions that reduced by 21.7% from INR1,452 crores to INR1,137 crores on a 
Y-o-Y basis. On a Q-on-Q basis, if we see this has broadly remained at the same level as we 
reported about INR1,144 crores in the last quarter. However, to point to note also here is that 
the provision for the current quarter also includes standard asset provision of about INR100 
crores on the FCNR backed loans. If we exclude this, then the provisions for the quarter declined 
by 9.3% on a Q-on-Q basis. 
 
The bank continues to hold the contingency provision of INR515 crores created last quarter. 
This is on a prudent basis, considering the evolving macroeconomic and the geopolitical 
uncertainties. In terms of credit cost translation, the credit cost for the quarter further improved 
to 1.38% as compared to 1.53% for the previous quarter. 
 
If we exclude the FCNR backed loans and the corresponding provision since these are backed 
by FD, the credit cost for the quarter would have been further lower to 1.30% on average funded 
assets. On an average total assets, the credit cost, which we have reported translates to a credit 
cost of 1.01%. 
 
Moving on to last few parts of my opening remarks. We all know that there has been a 
consultation paper, which has been issued by IRDAI. While this is still, as I said, in a 
consultation stage, there could be a draft circular which would come in followed by final 
regulations. And this is largely expected to come in from next year. 
 
But we have estimated the impact as is in the current form that if this has to come, this will 
definitely reduce our fee income. But we feel that, to a large extent, the impact can be offset by 
the expected repo increase and the FCNR benefit, which I have talked earlier. We will also 
continue to work on product mix changes and closely monitor the developments in this regard. 
 
Moving on to capital and liquidity. The capital adequacy ratio stood at 14.66% at September 
with CET1 ratio of 13.01%. On the LCR, the ratio was at 125% on an average for the quarter 
and with September being at higher at 139% because of the FCNR money, which came in 
towards the back end of August. Normally, as you would have noted, that normally, we have

So I can safely say that the trajectory is fairly established by now. This quarter on the core, 
without any adjustments, it is INR1,036 crores. So we feel good about that. I always said that

we had ROA of about 0.93%. Sudhanshu mentioned the FCNR in the denominator effect. But

for that. One is that the FCNR(B) deposits that we have raised is giving us about 1% benefit to 
the overall cost of funds, what we would have cost of deposits, what it would have cost us had

went up. So that will increase the yield on the books on the floating rate book. Deposit doesn't
